JMPD RECALL

By: Ntokozo Miya | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In an effort to clamp down on corruption, Joburg recruited 1500 carefully screened officers but after graduation, they were recalled - a training bungle that does not inspire confidence.

Unique Selling Point:
We speak to a JMPD metro police graduate who was among those recalled by the new Jhb mayor, citing training inadequacies. We also interrogate how this training blunder measures up in the city's fight against corruption and intentions to sway perceptions that metro officers are among the most corrupt in the country.

Summary:
Two years ago, the city of Johannesburg put out an advert for recruits for the metro police department. The aim was to put applicants through rigorous assessments and screenings to ensure that no one with a criminal record will slip through the cracks and end up on the force. This was especially important so that the city could dispel the perception that the JMPD is mostly corrupt. After having graduated last year, the recruits have since been recalled for training failures. What does this do for this city's image clean-up operation?

Further information:
We question authorities about how this embarrassing recall came to be, but more specifically, exactly how the corruption problem is addressed - are lifestyle audits conducted? measures put in place for whistleblowers in the public and in the force to be able to report corruption without concern that their identities will be exposed?

We also discuss recommendations by Corruption Watch on how the force can combat corruption within its ranks and the extent to which those recommendations are considered and implemented.

Hidden Identity Metro Police Graduate

JMPD RECALL SCRIPT - POST VIEWING FINAL
VO – Johannesburg - the centre of South Africa’s economy. With over 11 million registered vehicles, an alert police force is necessary to manage traffic in the city. But motorists say that for years, they’ve endured harassment and abuse at the hands of the Johannesburg Metro Police Department officers, who attempt to solicit bribes. 22 sec
UPSOUND
Officer asking for bribe
VO: The JMPD is the municipality’s enforcement arm for traffic management and crime prevention, but instead, scenes like this one have become synonymous with its officers. [this line refers to the video above]
VO: The JMPD’s deteriorating reputation led a Corruption Watch investigation in 2012. Its report “The Law for Sale” made several recommendations to eradicate graft. 22 sec
DAVID LEWIS - CORRUPTION WATCH
Sometimes it’s traffic cops stopping people who have committed no offence and attempting to extort money from them. They put their name tag and put the vest over the name tag and you can't read the name tag. The principal recommendation we made is that traffic cops should be obliged to show their identity.
VO – Nearly a decade later, Corruption Watch director David Lewis says officers who are not involved in shady activities should be reporting corrupt colleagues.
DAVID LEWIS – CORRUPTION WATCH – interview clip
People are scared. So what you need is the real support of your seniors. You need to know that...you’ll be treated as someone who’s done their duty rather than, pimped on their fellow cop.
VO – In 2017 former mayor Herman Mashaba recruited a thousand five hundred JMPD officers and insisted all candidates be vetted so that those selected would be men and women of integrity.
For eighteen months the new recruits were trained intensively. One thousand and eighty-five graduated in November.
Amid political turmoil in the DA, Mashaba resigned and was replaced by the ANC’s Geoffrey Makhubo.
After two months of active duty, the new recruits were recalled without explanation and sent back to training.
DAVID TEMBE - JMPD CHIEF
There was a lot of corruption during this recruitment.
VO – JMPD chief David Tembe doesn’t support the recall but admits that despite extensive screening some had to be disciplined for corruption.
DAVID TEMBE – JMPD CHIEF – xml timeline
Others claim that they paid some money, I think it was about R15 000, others paid R3000. People were arrested during the recruitment process.
VO - He insists that officials act decisively when mischief is exposed whether it’s among newcomers or veterans.
DAVID TEMBE – JMPD CHIEF – xml timeline
For the last three years, we have dismissed, we have about 169 cases and we have dismissed 74. But they are very few. The majority are good officers.
DAVID LEWIS – CORRUPTION WATCH
I think in Johannesburg in 1 week, you charge 3 or 4 drivers and 3 or 4 traffic officers with a serious criminal offence of corruption and put them away for it, I think it would plummet. I think here a good, highly-publicised trial and conviction would go a long way to stop it. We had reports of quite a lot of money involved. So, lifestyle audits might be valuable in overcoming that. (shots from “The Law for Sale” report)
VO – One of the graduates says anti-corruption measures were part of the training. We hide her identity to prevent victimisation.
JMPD GRADUATE – interview clip
With the JMPD, firstly they will teach you discipline. That is one thing that is emphasized day in day out.
VO – the recent recall was presented to the recruits as a matter of competence, rather than corruption.
LINK - JMPD graduates say they found out they were being recalled after seeing reports in the media... and as things stand, they have no idea what the future holds for them.
VO - It was also through the media that they learned that the drastic action was taken because they supposedly cannot direct traffic, handle guns or drive.
JMPD GRADUATE – interview clip
It sounded like a joke because you are going to find that more than half of students have got cars. We went to the shooting range whereby we were taught how to actually use firearms.
VO – She says some officers would need time to get used to managing traffic, but it didn't warrant a recall of the entire group.
While at the academy, the recruits got a stipend of around three thousand rands and after graduation, a salary of around twenty thousand rands per month.
JMPD GRADUATE – interview clip
We were enforcing by-laws. We were doing point duty. The traffic was now flowing nicely in Joburg because of us.
VO - Now out of training, and out of work, but still receiving salaries, officers sent us videos of themselves lounging around at the academy.
JMPD GRADUATE – interview clip
We don't do anything at all. At least if we were doing something that we know that it's under the word training, it was gonna make sense.
VO – At R20,900 a month for one thousand and eighty-five graduates, the city is spending nearly twenty-three million rands a month. With nothing to show for it.
LINK - This was a massive and costly decision, especially as we need more law enforcement officers visible around the city. The critical question is...who ordered the recall?
VO – Chief Tembe says he was satisfied with the competency level of the recruits.
DAVID TEMBE – JMPD CHIEF
CB – Chief, did you recall the JMPD graduates?
TEMBE – No, I did not recall them. I don't know why they were recalled because I was never informed.
CB - Should all these recruits have graduated?
TEMBE – Yes, because all steps were taken to ensure that they graduate. You won't get exam papers if you didn't meet all the requirements.


VO – New Johannesburg mayor Geoffrey Makhubo is in favour of the recall, but says he did not give the order.
GEOFFREY MAKHUBO – JOHANNESBURG MAYOR
MAYOR - It was not my decision. It was the academy's decision and I support it. I think when there are deficiencies in any product, the manufacturers can recall them.
VO – Both the mayor and the JMPD chief deny initiating the recall and to date, no other official has owned up to making the call.
Back in 2017, then MMC for Public Safety, Michael Sun oversaw the recruitment drive and see the recall as a political ploy to discredit the previous administration.
MICHAEL SUN – DA SHADOW MMC FOR PUBLIC SAFETY
We understand that when a new government comes in, they must do whatever they want to do to criticise the good work that was done previously but it is extremely dangerous to play with the lives of 1000 new officers who are now extremely disgruntled.
VO - He feels there should be extensive consultations before such a recall.
MICHAEL SUN – DA SHADOW MMC FOR PUBLIC SAFETY
“You need to explain to us - what prompted the decision, what assessments have you done, ... and very importantly, ... when is this retraining going to start, when is it going to end and how much is it going to cost the city?”
JMPD GRADUATE – interview clip
CB - Do you feel that you've been caught in political crossfire?
Yes, we have, big time. Because someone is trying to prove that a certain government is better than a certain government and it's wrong.
LINK - The new Johannesburg mayor denies that a recall of more than a thousand JMPD graduates is a political move and says his aim is to get more competent officers on the beat.
GEOFFREY MAKHUBO – JOHANNESBURG MAYOR
I don't have time to be discrediting that administration, I'm looking forward. ... I don't want the people of Johannesburg to be questioning the competency of the city's officers.
VO - Officers’ capabilities remain a concern. Motorists complain about police failure to effectively respond to congestion during load shedding. Some said it's common to see a road block set up on busy roads during peak traffic hours. ('LATEST JMPD” folder with FB screen grabs about this)
Tembe says with less political interference and more cooperation between the JMPD and municipal authorities, the state of affairs in the city's police force can improve.
DAVID TEMBE – JMPD CHIEF
CB – You must be concerned about the reputation of the JMPD, will this recall have a further adverse effect?
TEMBE – Ja, it will have an adverse effect if the chief is not in charge. If the chief is in charge, he will be able to turn it around.
CB – But you say if the chief is in charge so who is in charge?
TEMBE – [laughs] Do you really want to know? [laughs] I don't think so.
CB – Are you saying the mayor is ruling the roost?
TEMBE – I don't know. It's the first time in the history of my life that all of a sudden, things are happening, I am not there.
OUTRO – Since the recall, graduates have not been told what training they lack, when they will get re-trained, and how long it will go on for.
JMPD ACADEMY GRADUATE
I'm not happy at all because I have not been informed as to what's actually happening. ... I'm just confused.

PROMOS

The JMPD officers recalled over training concerns say they are qualified to be on active duty and demand answers for being sent back to the academy.

Over a thousand JMPD graduates recalled after just two months of active duty - were they caught in a political crossfire between the old and new city administration?

Will the recall of more than one thousand JMPD graduates tarnish the reputation of the police force? We ask: who gave the order and why?

It's the first time in the history of my life that all of a sudden, things are happening, I am not there. OUTRO – Since the recall, graduates have not been told what training they lack, when they will get re-trained, and how long it will go on for. JMPD ACADEMY GRADUATE I'm not happy at all because I have not been informed as to what's actually happening. ... I'm just confused. PROMOS The JMPD officers recalled over training concerns say they are qualified to be on active duty and demand answers for being sent back to the academy. Over a thousand JMPD graduates recalled after just two months of active duty - were they caught in a political crossfire between the old and new city administration? Will the recall of more than one thousand JMPD graduates tarnish the reputation of the police force? We ask: who gave the order and why?

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): In an effort to clamp down on corruption, Joburg recruited 1500 carefully screened officers but after graduation, they were recalled - a training bungle that does not inspire confidence.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We speak to a JMPD metro police graduate who was among those recalled by the new Jhb mayor, citing training inadequacies. We also interrogate how this training blunder measures up in the city's fight against corruption and intentions to sway perceptions that metro officers are among the most corrupt in the country.
metadata.Summary: Two years ago, the city of Johannesburg put out an advert for recruits for the metro police department. The aim was to put applicants through rigorous assessments and screenings to ensure that no one with a criminal record will slip through the cracks and end up on the force. This was especially important so that the city could dispel the perception that the JMPD is mostly corrupt. After having graduated last year, the recruits have since been recalled for training failures. What does this do for this city's image clean-up operation?
metadata.Further information: We question authorities about how this embarrassing recall came to be, but more specifically, exactly how the corruption problem is addressed - are lifestyle audits conducted? measures put in place for whistleblowers in the public and in the force to be able to report corruption without concern that their identities will be exposed? We also discuss recommendations by Corruption Watch on how the force can combat corruption within its ranks and the extent to which those recommendations are considered and implemented.
